question.answer: The concept should be applied through a staged pathway: preserve and study traditional knowledge, test claims through rigorous interdisciplinary research, enforce quality and regulatory safeguards, and translate only validated findings into accessible care. Collaboration can build capacity, but announcements or publications alone do not prove clinical efficacy.

sections.heading: AIIA’s institutional moment
paragraphs: On 17 October 2026, the All India Institute of Ayurveda marked its 10th Foundation Day while KAUMARACON 2026 concluded with deliberations on Ayurvedic child healthcare [P1]. The programme therefore connected institutional development with a specialised healthcare domain.
The source reports two MoUs: one with Rashtriya Ayurved Vidyapeeth and another with Arogya Bharati, intended to strengthen institutional collaboration and knowledge-sharing in Ayurveda [P1].

sections.heading: From knowledge-sharing to accountable translation
paragraphs: The conference discussed scientific validation, interdisciplinary research, preventive care and regulatory frameworks in Traditional, Complementary and Integrative Medicine [P1]. These themes matter because research findings must be converted into safe, reliable and appropriately regulated healthcare practices.

More than 15 academic publications and educational resources were launched, along with a research-methodology and medical-statistics textbook, an entrepreneurship course for Ayush professionals and a new website [P1]. Their practical consequence is potentially stronger learning and research capacity, but the source does not establish the effectiveness of any treatment or the reach of these resources.
